summary:
KEPLER (Lunar Landing & Horizon Decision Studio) is a terrain-aware mission planning platform designed to help astronauts and mission planners evaluate landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole.

We developed an interactive 3D lunar environment that combines NASA’s LOLA elevation data and SPICE ephemeris information to simulate surface illumination, terrain-obstructed sunlight, Earth visibility, communication windows, and solar power availability. Its Mission Control dashboard provides real-time mission metrics, while Horizon Replay allows users to compare landing sites and examine changing conditions over time. Science Explorer demonstrates how lunar terrain and curvature affect sunlight and communication line-of-sight.

KEPLER addresses a critical challenge in lunar exploration: a location that appears illuminated or suitable on a flat map may actually be shadowed or lose communication because of surrounding terrain and the Moon’s curvature. By making these constraints visible and measurable, KEPLER supports more informed landing-site selection, mission scheduling, and power planning. This is important for improving astronaut safety, operational reliability, and the success of future lunar missions.
details:
KEPLER (Lunar Landing & Horizon Decision Studio) is an interactive mission-planning platform designed to help evaluate potential landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole.

How it works:
KEPLER combines NASA’s LOLA elevation data with NAIF SPICE ephemeris information to create a terrain-aware lunar environment. Its Python backend calculates topocentric vectors and terrain horizon angles on demand, evaluating sunlight availability, terrain obstruction, and Earth communication line-of-sight. The scientific implementation is supported by 17 verified unit and scientific tests.

The platform includes:

  • Mission Control: Displays Sun and Earth elevation, terrain clearance, solar power availability, communication status, and mission operating states.
  • Horizon Replay: Compares landing sites and visualises changing illumination and communication conditions over time.
  • Science Explorer: Demonstrates how obstacle distance, terrain height, lunar curvature, and antenna mast height affect visibility.
  • Lunar Experience: Provides an interactive 3D view of the Moon and candidate landing regions.
  • Decision Support: Helps assess landing-site robustness, blackout periods, illumination windows, and battery requirements.

Tools and technologies:
The frontend uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js. The backend uses Python and FastAPI. Scientific data sources include NASA LOLA elevation datasets and NAIF SPICE ephemeris kernels. The interface follows a minimalist, pitch-black (#000000) luxury design language, avoiding neon colours, unnecessary icons, and visual clutter.

Benefits, creativity, and intended impact:
KEPLER brings terrain, illumination, communication, and power analysis into one interactive decision-making environment. Unlike simplified visualisations that may overlook local terrain obstruction, it considers the lunar horizon and spherical curvature when evaluating visibility. This helps mission planners identify hidden risks, compare landing locations, and make better-informed operational decisions. By translating complex scientific calculations into accessible visual simulations, KEPLER aims to support safer, more reliable, and more efficient future lunar missions.
